chains.title: XBP1 loss-of-binding at an unannotated element perturbs PELI2 in MCF7

links.claim: QBiC-SELEX group G382 is an XBP1 own-model bZIP model with z -91.69 and effect -3.167, so alt T binds XBP1 less strongly than ref C. XBP1 is the own-model TF named in this group. Cellular occupancy is not supported by the available ENCODE XBP1 ChIP-seq data in MCF7: no peak contains the variant, though absence may also reflect no XBP1 experiment in that biosample.

The variant is an intron_variant with no annotated regulatory feature, no overlapping cCRE, and the nearest dELS is 1868 bp away. This chain therefore requires an unannotated or cryptic XBP1-responsive element; the current epigenomic evidence is negative for a canonical element.

PELI2 is the nearest protein-coding gene at 230.8 kb, but there is no breast mammary tissue eQTL for this variant and the only Open Targets molecular QTL is a weak brain eQTL for ENSG00000259868 with PIP 0.03, not PELI2. The variant-to-PELI2 link is therefore speculative and long-range.

XBP1 is expressed at 636.57 TPM in the MCF7/ACH-000019 expression context, so an allele-specific XBP1 effect is cell-type plausible in principle. However, no ENCODE XBP1 ChIP-seq peak containing this variant is reported in MCF7, so cellular occupancy at this site remains untested or unsupported.

PELI2 is a Pellino-family E3 ubiquitin ligase and has appeared among prognostic genes in a cancer bioinformatics model, but the supplied literature does not connect rs11629191 or PELI2 to breast cancer. The phenotype link is indirect.

predictions: Ref C binds XBP1 more strongly than alt T at the variant.
If the variant is in a functional XBP1 element, XBP1 perturbation in MCF7 should change PELI2 or nearby-locus expression.
The variant should sit in an accessible regulatory element in MCF7 despite current negative cCRE annotation.
falsified_if: XBP1 does not bind the ref allele more strongly than alt T at this sequence in vitro or in cells.
XBP1 perturbation in MCF7 does not alter PELI2 or nearby-locus expression.
The variant lies in closed chromatin with no regulatory activity in breast cancer cells.

chains.title: CREB3L4 loss-of-binding at the variant affects a nearby breast-cancer locus

links.claim: QBiC-SELEX group G017 contains CREB3, CREB3L1, CREB3L2 and CREB3L4 own models; the best model is CREB3 with effect -1.64, and CREB3L4 is a passing own-model member with z -37.55, consistent with alt T binding less than ref C. The CREB3L4-specific effect is not directly shown. No ENCODE CREB3L4 ChIP-seq peak contains the variant in MCF7, although absence may reflect no experiment.

No cCRE overlaps the variant, no SCREEN cCRE lies within 500 bp, and the nearest dELS is 1868 bp away. This chain posits a non-canonical CREB3L4-responsive element rather than a validated ENCODE cCRE; the current epigenomic evidence is negative.

PELI2 is only the nearest protein-coding gene at 230.8 kb. There is no significant breast mammary tissue eQTL at this variant, and the only Open Targets molecular QTL is a weak brain eQTL for ENSG00000259868 with PIP 0.03, not PELI2. The gene assignment is weak.

CREB3L4 is expressed at 48.8 TPM in the MCF7/ACH-000019 expression context, supporting potential activity in this cell line. However, no ENCODE CREB3L4 ChIP-seq peak containing the variant is reported in MCF7, so cellular occupancy is not established.

A CREB3L4-dependent change in PELI2 could plausibly touch cancer biology through Pellino-family signaling, but the supplied breast-cancer evidence is indirect and does not link this variant, CREB3L4, or PELI2 to breast cancer.

predictions: Ref C binds CREB3L4 more strongly than alt T at the variant, if CREB3L4 itself is the relevant group member.
CREB3L4 perturbation in MCF7 should change PELI2 or nearby-locus expression.
The variant should act through an unannotated CREB3L4-responsive element in MCF7.
falsified_if: CREB3L4 does not bind the ref allele more strongly than alt T in vitro or in cells.
CREB3L4 perturbation in MCF7 has no effect on PELI2 or nearby gene expression.
The variant is not in an accessible regulatory element in MCF7.

chains.title: CREB1 loss-of-binding at a weak distal element alters a nearby locus

links.claim: QBiC-SELEX group G062 is a bZIP group with CREB1 and CREM own models; CREB1 is the best model with z -37.47 and effect -2.019, so alt T binds less than ref C. CREB1 is chosen over CREM because it has the stronger passing model and higher MCF7 expression.

The variant has no annotated regulatory feature and no overlapping cCRE, and the nearest dELS is 1868 bp away. A functional CREB1 element would have to be unannotated or poorly captured; the current epigenomic evidence is negative.

PELI2 is the nearest protein-coding gene at 230.8 kb, but no breast mammary tissue eQTL links this variant to PELI2, and the only Open Targets molecular QTL is a weak brain eQTL for ENSG00000259868 with PIP 0.03. The target-gene link is speculative.
CREB1 is expressed at 30.28 TPM in the MCF7/ACH-000019 expression context, so an allele-specific CREB1 effect is cell-type plausible.

This chain would require CREB1-dependent regulation of a Pellino-family gene to influence breast cancer. The supplied literature establishes the Pellino-family context but does not connect CREB1 to PELI2 or to rs11629191 in breast cancer.

predictions: Ref C binds CREB1 more strongly than alt T at the variant.
CREB1 perturbation in MCF7 should change PELI2 or nearby-locus expression if this chain is correct.
The variant should have allele-dependent regulatory activity in breast cancer cells despite negative cCRE annotation.
